messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Serbian (Latin script), guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Serbian (Latin script) line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Bih bio pesnik i pevao o tom pravednom. sin Ankise koji je došao iz Troje. nakon što je ponosni Ilion bio spaljen.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (semantic role) | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|----------------------------------------|----------------------|------------------------|--------| | Poeta | speaker’s artistic identity (subject) | pesnik | poet | OK | | fui | identity predicate “was” (1 sg past) | **Bih bio** | *would be* (conditional) | **WRONG** (tense/aspect mismatch) | | e | coordinator “and” | i | and | OK | | cantai | past action “sang” | pevao | sang | OK | | di | preposition “of/about” (object of singing) | o | about/of | OK | | quel | demonstrative “that” (specifies noun) | tom | that (masc.) | OK | | giusto | property “just” (adjective) | pravednom | just | OK | | figliuol | son (male child) | sin | son | OK | | d'Anchise | genitive “of Anchises” (parent‑child) | Ankise | of Anchises | OK | | che (rel.) | relative pronoun “who” | koji | who | OK | | venne | motion “came” (from Troy) | došao | came | OK | | di (source) | preposition “from” (origin) | iz | from | OK | | Troia | proper name “Troy” | Troje | Troy | OK | | poi | temporal adverb “after” | nakon | after | OK | | che (subord.) | conjunction “that” introducing result clause | što | that (introducing clause) | OK | | 'l | definite article “the” (definite determiner) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (Serbian lacks articles) | | superbo | attribute “proud” (adjective) | ponosni | proud | OK | | Ilïón | proper name “Ilion” (city) | Ilion | Ilion | OK | | fu | auxiliary forming passive “had been” | bio | was (aux.) | OK | | combusto | past participle “burned” (passive) | spaljen | burned | OK |

### Issues Detected - **WRONG:** *fui* → “Bih bio”. The Italian past “fui” should be rendered with a past form in Serbian (e.g., **“Bio sam”**). “Bih bio” is conditional, not past. - **UNNECESSARY:** *'l* (definite article). Serbian does not use articles, so the article is correctly omitted.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Serbian (Latin script) script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Serbian (Latin script) text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
